name: Steerable Pyramid Decomposition
description: Applies steerable pyramid for orientation-selective sub-band analysis — detects AI texture synthesis artifacts (Simoncelli & Freeman, 1995).
mechanism:
This method applies the Steerable Pyramid decomposition by Simoncelli & Freeman (1995) for multi-scale oriented forensic analysis:

1. **Pyramid Construction**: The image is decomposed via steerable filters into oriented subbands at multiple scales. Unlike the DWT, the steerable pyramid is non-aliased, translation-invariant, and provides exact rotation steerability — enabling analysis at arbitrary orientations without recomputation.

2. **Subband Statistics Extraction**: At each scale and orientation, local coefficient statistics are computed: variance, kurtosis, skewness, and the parameters of a fitted generalized Gaussian distribution. Natural images produce characteristic heavy-tailed distributions in oriented subbands.

3. **Cross-Scale Phase Analysis**: Phase relationships between coefficients at adjacent scales reveal edge structure. Natural edges maintain coherent phase across scales following the predictions of local spectral analysis. AI-generated images may exhibit phase incoherence at generation boundaries or fine scales.

4. **Orientation Energy Analysis**: The orientation energy at each scale E(θ,s) = Σ|c(θ,s)|² captures directional texture structure. Natural images show smooth orientation energy as a function of angle, while AI generation artifacts often produce anomalous peaks or gaps in the orientation energy function.

5. **Texture Synthesis Detection**: The joint statistics of steerable pyramid coefficients (parent-child correlations, cross-orientation coupling) define a texture signature per Portilla & Simoncelli (2000). AI-generated textures often fail to reproduce the full joint statistics achievable by the steerable pyramid model, enabling detection of synthetic content.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models

references.title: Simoncelli, E.P. & Freeman, W.T. (1995). The Steerable Pyramid: A Flexible Architecture for Multi-Scale Derivative Computation. IEEE ICIP.
Portilla, J. & Simoncelli, E.P. (2000). A Parametric Texture Model Based on Joint Statistics of Complex Wavelet Coefficients. IJCV.
